_README: Configuration for the figure-text translation pipeline. Status lives in REGISTER.md; how-to lives in README.md; this file holds only values the code reads.
_suffix: NOT SET HERE ON PURPOSE. The translated-filename suffix is owned by tools/generate-image-mapping.js (DEFAULT_SUFFIX) and pinned by its test against the committed corpus. Restating it here would be a second source of truth.
_renderDpi: OpenStax rendered the published jpgs at exactly 200 dpi from these same PDFs (verified pixel-exact, 468x275.642pt -> 1300x766). Rendering at any other dpi breaks check.py's oracle comparison.
_outputFormat: SETTLED 2026-09-02 by measurement in a real browser inside - see REGISTER.md item 5. SVG loses 0.27px on layout fidelity (invisible), ties at ZERO on selectable text (an -loaded SVG contributes 0 chars to the DOM), and wins decisively on sharpness at 2x and on size (2.8x). The embedded subset font is load-bearing: stripping it changes 4.2% of pixels.
_editionPrecedence: The OpenStax delivery is TWO trees: all 1st-edition images, and a second tree holding ONLY images updated or added for the 2nd edition. A figure present in the updates tree MUST be sourced from there; the 1st-edition tree is the fallback. Getting this backwards silently translates a superseded illustration. Enforced by sources.py, not by this comment.

_supersededArtwork: Basenames whose ONLY available vector is known to be superseded by the published figure. sources.py refuses these before any lookup, so they report `unresolved` and nothing is composed or published for them - deliberately, because an untranslated correct figure beats a translated wrong one, and unresolved stays counted and named. The value is the REASON and is required: an entry nobody can later evaluate is a permanent unexplained hole. Matched after the lookup's case and punctuation fold (sources._normkey). ⚠️ This list is HAND-VERIFIED, not a detector output. An aspect-ratio scan flags 38 chemistry figures at >25% disagreement with the published raster, but its precision is UNKNOWN (a crop, a padded bounding box or a multi-panel composite all produce the same signal), so a figure belongs here only once a human has looked at both. ⚠️ A refusal does not retire an EARLIER translated copy: where a June `_IS.svg` and image-mapping row exist, readers keep seeing that copy, and the driver names it (§C140 ⑦).

_retiredFigures: §C140 ㊵. Basenames whose TRANSLATED COPY was retired by a [USER] ruling: readers get OpenStax's own figure, and no run may make a translated copy again. sources.py refuses these first — before supersededArtwork and before any lookup — as `retired`; tools/generate-image-mapping.js never maps them; tools/retire-translated-figure.js removes their image-mapping row and translated copy (--retire), and later their published copies once nothing references them (--prune). Different from supersededArtwork, which is about the SOURCE drawing: a figure may be in both (BlastFurn, Ques11ans). The value is what was ruled and why, over 40 characters. An entry lands in the commit that runs the retire, never earlier. The JS tools match a key exactly; sources.py folds case and punctuation; tools/lib/figure-config-validate.js requires each key to be exactly one book's image basename.
_artworkPins: §C140 ㊵. {basename: {kind, edition, file, reason}}: the ONE file a figure's artwork is taken from. `edition` is a key of this book's trees in sources.local.json; `file` is a path inside that tree, never a stem or a pattern. kind `alias` fills a hole in the delivery, and is refused as pin-conflict once any file matches the basename, exactly or folded. kind `override` deliberately replaces the normal lookup. A missing file is refused as pin-missing, never a fall-back; a malformed entry as pin-invalid; two pins naming one file as pin-conflict. A pin lands in the commit that runs its buy, after tools/lib/figure-config-validate.js passes locally: CI runs only after the money is spent.
_paperSizes: Standard paper sizes in points, [width, height], matched in either orientation within paperTolerancePt. A candidate whose page box is one of these is a production page - a placement or dialogue SHEET - not a figure: sources.py skips it for the edition's next candidate, and refuses the figure only when every candidate in the edition is one; tools/figure-run.js reads the same table to name a live translated copy whose SVG viewBox is a whole sheet (§C140 ⑦). THIS FILE IS THE TABLE'S ONLY OWNER: neither sources.py nor figure-run.js restates a size. Measured 2026-09-16, before that per-candidate rule (evidence/2026-09-16-c7-explore/): exactly 2 of 910 resolved artworks were paper-size, both Letter (rvosmosis, N2O5); on 2026-10-01, before any ㊵ retirement, only rvosmosis was refused, because N2O5's .eps sibling resolved.
_paperTolerancePt: How far, in points, a width or height may differ from a paperSizes entry and still match it. Measured 2026-09-16 (evidence/2026-09-16-c7-explore/): still exactly the same 2 at ±10 pt; the next largest artwork is 468x576 pt.
_sourceTreesFile: Local absolute paths live in a gitignored file because they are machine-specific. Copy sources.local.json.example and fill it in.
